rule: An incident is closed only when its original reproduction fails, the corrected path passes, and the evidence is repeatable.

incidents.reproduction: A visible start/regenerate/stop button has no reachable request and state transition.
incidents.guard: Every interactive control has a success case and a disabled-or-failure case.

incidents.reproduction: The UI reports Codex connected when only the page or Bridge is reachable.
incidents.guard: Surface, Bridge, CLI discovery, authentication, model schema probe and Skill readiness remain separate.

incidents.reproduction: Typing a topic changes generated content or final output before model completion.
incidents.guard: Only a validated model response may create a working revision.

incidents.reproduction: A cached or late result overwrites a newer topic, manual edit, annotation or graph.
incidents.guard: Write-back requires run ID, execution-plan hash, input-snapshot hash and current revision CAS.

incidents.reproduction: Annotation regeneration reads the previous generated draft but drops the current human-edited draft.
incidents.guard: currentDraft is authoritative and every active annotation receives a receipt.

incidents.reproduction: A connected DNA node runs without the original skill, confirmed corpus snapshot or immutable artifact.
incidents.guard: Missing original distillation evidence blocks execution; no summary-rule fallback exists.

incidents.reproduction: One model writes a draft, self-reports 95 or 100, and releases it without independent review.
incidents.guard: Two independent reviews target one frozen draft; release score is the conservative minimum and hard vetoes override it.

incidents.reproduction: A test searches page source for button labels and is reported as UI E2E.
incidents.guard: Static source tests are labelled static; publication requires an isolated real-browser run against the Bridge.

incidents.reproduction: A model appears selectable although it is missing, unconfigured, unreachable or cannot satisfy the schema.
incidents.guard: Writer and Reviewer profiles expose installed/configured/reachable/schemaProbe/ready independently.

incidents.reproduction: An editorial or detector score is shown as the probability that a human wrote the text.
incidents.guard: The product calls it an editorial release score and treats external detectors as optional side signals only.

incidents.reproduction: A long model task is declared failed at the old HTTP timeout while its process is still running.
incidents.guard: Model stages have no application wall-clock deadline; the run remains queryable and only an explicit matching cancel may stop it.

incidents.reproduction: A saved build, URL query parameter, Git tag or local marker is reported as a deployed release.
incidents.guard: local_candidate, validated, tagged and deployed are separately evidenced states.

incidents.reproduction: A necessary professional list, model number, formula, unit or ordinary Chinese phrase is blocked as AI flavor.
incidents.guard: Single tokens never hard-veto; grouped patterns require positive, negative and adversarial cases.

incidents.reproduction: The start button shows a forbidden cursor without a visible reason or recovery action.
incidents.guard: Every blocker exposes a stable code, node id, Chinese explanation and recovery action, and the server enforces the same gate.

incidents.reproduction: An unavailable selected model silently falls back to another model while the UI keeps the old label.
incidents.guard: Provider and model profile are hashed and receipted; unavailable profiles fail closed and late results are rejected.

incidents.reproduction: Specific numbers, models, quotes or cases pass review without a frozen evidence link.
incidents.guard: Every verifiable claim is supported, an explicit assumption or unsupported; unsupported claims hard-veto.

incidents.reproduction: A browser disconnect, refresh or Bridge restart loses the status or result of an ordinary writing run.
incidents.guard: Writing runs use a persistent ledger, restart marks interrupted state, cancel kills only the exact process tree and late output cannot commit.

incidents.reproduction: An untrusted web origin, prompt-injected reference or disguised local file crosses the Bridge boundary.
incidents.guard: Origin/session gates, prompt-data separation, secret redaction and file-content/path checks fail closed.

incidents.reproduction: A newly added structured-output property is marked locally optional, so OpenAI rejects the entire schema before writing begins.
incidents.guard: Every property of every closed object in the model-facing schema is required; optional Bridge-owned values are nullable instead of omitted.

incidents.reproduction: A reviewer honestly returns humanized=false and the Bridge treats it as malformed output rather than a review-required candidate.
incidents.guard: The contract accepts both boolean values; false is retained and closes the quality gate without discarding a structurally valid draft.

incidents.reproduction: An initial run has no annotations, but the model invents a receipt and the Bridge discards the whole draft.
incidents.guard: When the server-owned annotation ID set is empty, receipts are deterministically normalized to an empty array; non-empty annotation runs remain exact and strict.

incidents.reproduction: Writer and both reviewers each regenerate one large delivery-shaped object, causing a 300-character smoke run to take more than fifteen minutes.
incidents.guard: Use stage-specific schemas and receipts, expose review_a/review_b timing, and benchmark each model/reasoning profile before calling the quick workflow usable.
